1 Load data

all.sample.info <- read.csv(file = file.path(here::here(), "data", "vcf_data", "all.sample.info.csv"), sep=";", header=FALSE)

dim(all.sample.info)
[1] 27  3
rownames(all.sample.info) <-  all.sample.info[, 1]

## Load sample names with no filter on q20
vcf_path <- file.path(here::here(), "data", "vcf_data", "wRI.vcf.gz")
#vcf_path <- file.path(here::here(), "data", "vcf_data", "wRI.filtered.vcf.gz")
## Name of samples
seq.names <- unlist(strsplit(grep("^#CHROM", readLines(vcf_path), value = TRUE), "\t"))
seq.names <- seq.names[-(1:9)]

2 Select samples

samples <- c("Col-FR-Bal001", "Col-FR-Ren000", "Col-IT-Tre000", "Iso-FR-Par006", "D-sub", "CN-Kun_KM5" , "IT_Tre_Om300", "US-CA_wRI_Dsim2", "ZB_wRI_Dsim1" )

## Filter CI individuals
wSuz.pooldata <- poolfstat::pooldata.subset(pooldata=wSuz.pooldata,  pool.index = which(rownames(all.sample.info)%in% samples))
Data consists of 696 SNPs for 9 Pools
## Export genotypes
geno_data <- round(wSuz.pooldata@refallele.readcount/wSuz.pooldata@readcoverage, 2)

## Add positions
geno_data <- data.frame(wSuz.pooldata@snp.info, geno_data)
colnames(geno_data) <- wSuz.pooldata@poolnames

3 Check MAF across samples

As expected from the presence of a single Wolbachia genotype, the MAF boxplot on the called SNPs shows a reduced genetic diversity in Individual, Iso-female and Colony sample (Figure 1). Still, some polymorphism is found at some SNPs (this may also be related to coverage heterogeneity)?

4 Check call rate

## The 98 SNPs of the 7 samples are well covered
ind.callrate <- apply(wSuz.pooldata@readcoverage, 2, function(x) sum(x != 0)/nrow(wSuz.pooldata@readcoverage))

hist(snp.callrate)
## Filter XX SNPs with fewer than 90% of individual samples covered
wSuz.pooldata <- poolfstat::pooldata.subset(pooldata=wSuz.pooldata,  snp.index = which(snp.callrate>0.9))
Data consists of 549 SNPs for 9 Pools

5 PCA and clustering

5.1 PCA

set.seed(1234)
par(xpd=TRUE)
res.pca <- poolfstat::randomallele.pca(x = wSuz.pooldata, plot.pcs = c(1, 2), return.snploadings = TRUE)

## Hirarchical clustering equivalent to UPGMA
tt <- hclust(as.dist(fstats@pairwise.div), method= "average")
plot(tt)
## Neighbor joining distance
tt <- ape::nj(as.dist(fstats@pairwise.div))
plot(tt)
#quartz()
## Heatmap
heatmap(fstats@pairwise.div, distfun = as.dist)
## With ComplexHeatmap
div.hm <- ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(fstats@pairwise.div,
cluster_rows =TRUE,cluster_columns=TRUE,name="Divergence",
show_heatmap_legend=FALSE,column_title = "Divergence (1-Q2)")

div.hm

6 Cif genes TODO Sveta (please check that there is no coverage information in the second copy of WO-B at position 1,071,000 to 1,142,000)

Conner et al 2017 wRi, there are two nearly identical copies (99.4%) of WO-B, from about 565,000 : 636,000 and from about 1,071,000 to 1,142,000 https://www.genome.jp/dbget-bin/www_bget?refseq+NC_012416

Type I cifA WRI_RS02675 WRi_005370 in wRI 571723:573147 cifB WRI_RS07690 WRi_p05380 in WRI: 573223:576723 (stop codon in wRI)

Type I cifA WRI_RS05040 WRi_010030 in wRI 1078182:1079606 cifB WRI_RS07735 WRi_p10040 in WRI: 1079682:1083182 (stop codon in wRI)

Type II cifA WRI_RS03370 WRi_006720 in wRI 728237:729607 (partial with insertion at 729284 in wSuz) cifB WRI_RS03365 WRi_006710 in WRI: 725963:728227

## Thoughts on the lack of CI:
## 5 mutations in Type I cifB between wSuz and wMel (some of them shared with wSuz)
## inactivation of Type II cifA by a transposase in wSuz and wSpc but not in wRI (Conner et al 2017)

data <- read.table(file=here::here("data/derived_data/wol_genotypes.csv"), sep=";", header = TRUE)
